title: JANUS Engine — dedicated research-branch manifest

latest_findings.magnetic_baseline: Coreless/slotless AFPM starter-generator remains the preferred first Axle drive; micro-EPM remains an A/B assist branch only if it reduces total startup Wh after switching losses.
latest_findings.magnetic_field_metrology: The project now requires synchronized Bx/By/Bz mapping versus encoder angle, RPM, current, torque and temperature in static-PM, passive-spin, motor, generator and optional EPM states.
latest_findings.copper_vs_brass: NIST conductivity anchors put copper around 57 MS/m and brass C260 around 15.5 MS/m. A brass-class non-ferromagnetic structural Axle is therefore the preliminary electromagnetic preference because it should support weaker eddy currents than copper for comparable geometry, but the exact alloy must pass corrosion/dezincification, mechanical and wet-chemistry tests.
latest_findings.co_rotating_field_rule: The PM field rigidly attached to the Axle is approximately static in the rotor frame; eddy losses are driven mainly by relative time-varying stator fields, harmonics/asymmetry, EPM pulses and stationary conductive structures exposed to the rotating field.
latest_findings.skin_depth_screen: For 4-8 pole-pair examples over 60-600 RPM, representative skin depths are millimetres to centimetres; a few-mm copper/brass Axle is not a perfect magnetic shield but still requires eddy-drag/heating measurement.
latest_findings.journal_policy: JANUS Engine now has an append-only project development journal separate from the global restoration journal.

next_actions: Freeze pole count, magnet grade/dimensions, air gap and coil-current envelope for first AFPM bench article.
Perform equal-geometry copper-versus-brass magnetic A/B with 3-axis field, encoder, current, torque and temperature synchronized.
Measure stray field at chamber wall, POMS boundary and outside housing.
Use measured field/loss maps to choose Axle material and only then optimize EPM timing or field shaping.
Append every design decision and reversal to the project development journal.
